assessments.reasoning: The Index’s pinned scope includes relevant data licenses and earlier editions. The v1 text identifies the edition, rights granted and covered copyright or database-right information.

The Archives served the English HTML at /doc/open-government-licence/version/1/open-government-licence.htm. Its full digest matches the claim. Bytes [8586,8636) declare version 1.0. The grant, attribution example and Controller of HMSO provenance agree. The interoperability passage is contextual.

The pinned Index decision, bytes [4398,4601), binds 80723b70ab4c4af19bb99a69a85fa64b, Open Government Licence v1.0 (UK), ogl-uk-1-0, sha256:a5ddab8cb10dacfd82f9e3f6699191849d62e74180525ec5041572c408a8c2ca, license and active.

challenge.method: Checked whether the generic HTML title, latest-version link or the v2 page could establish v1 identity, and whether the existence of v2 implied a historical Index state for v1.
challenge.results: The v1 body supplies a v1.0 attribution notice, explicit version declaration and permission to continue using information licensed under that version. The v2 body declares a different edition. The decision expressly maintains both references as active.

limitations: The publisher HTML says “His Majesty’s Stationery Office.” The reported monarch-wording discrepancy with SPDX limits textual equivalence. The SPDX specimen was outside the listed originals.
The publisher permits continued use of information licensed under v1. A particular work’s coverage, redistribution rights and installation eligibility require separate evidence.
Index active concerns lookup. It establishes neither publisher currency nor SPDX deprecation status. Consumer release authorization is separate.
reasoning: The National Archives’ version 1 HTML expressly declares OGL v1.0 and grants conditional use of information. The Index taxonomy covers that grant. Its decision records the v1 entity as active independently of the v2 and v3 entries.
